nodes.summary: For all bit strings $x$ and $w$, the answer of the SAT host with flag true on $(x, w)$ is the conjunction of two bits. The first is false if the complete length-prefixed CNF decoder fails on $x$; if $x$ decodes to a CNF formula $\varphi$, it is true exactly when every clause of $\varphi$ has at most three literals. The second is the return value of the SAT verifier on $(x, w)$.
nodes.title: Answer of the SAT host with the three-literal filter

nodes.summary: CNF satisfiability is NP-complete: the decision problem accepting exactly the bit strings that encode a satisfiable CNF formula is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
